title: priority-shepherd-v2-and-soft-evictor-regional-circuit-companion-hotfix
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes:
- Introduces Priority Shepherd v2: improved tenant-aware shedding and graceful soft-eviction.
- Adds a regional circuit companion that coordinates soft fallbacks across zones.
- Hotfixes KV-preserve regression observed during rapid regional failovers.
description:
Motivation: In recent incidents (SUP-914) we observed that aggressive global shedding caused tenant starvation and inconsistent KV preservation when regions flapped. This PR introduces Priority Shepherd v2 (PSv2) — a graded, tenant-aware admission controller that cooperates with a new soft-evictor and a lightweight regional-circuit companion to achieve predictable SLO behavior during overload and region failovers.

Summary of changes: PSv2 implements a multi-tranche priority curve (high/medium/low) with a decay window so tenants ramp back smoothly; it supports soft-eviction markers that preserve KV cache prefixes for warm rejoin; the regional-circuit companion broadcasts compact circuit-state deltas (open/hedging/quiet) to nearby zones to allow coordinated, low-latency fallbacks instead of blind hard rejects. A small fallback policy was added to the router to prefer warm-compatible model variants in adjacent regions when a circuit moves to hedging.

Why this is different: Unlike previous one-shot shedder patches, PSv2 focuses on temporal smoothing (decay + probation) and KV-preservation semantics, reducing noisy rejections and recovery spikes. The regional-circuit companion is intentionally compact to avoid additional control-plane load and uses the existing heartbeat channel.

Files and modules touched (high-level): srv/shedder/priority_shepherd_v2.go, srv/shedder/soft_evictor.go, srv/router/fallback_policy.go, infra/telemetry/telemetry_tags.go, tests/integ/regional_fallback_test.go, docs/ops/priority_shepherd_v2.md, tools/upgrade/checklist.sh, pkg/kv/kv_preserve.go

Compatibility & rollout: Default behavior is gated behind a feature flag (feature.priority_shepherd_v2) and off for Dedicated customers by default. Rollout plan: canary in us-west-2 -> expanded to one additional region -> global. The feature flag supports dynamic params (tranche thresholds and decay windows) to tune during rollout.

Testing performed: unit tests for priority bucketing and decay functions; integration tests simulate regional flaps and assert KV prefix preservation and end-to-end latency SLOs; a small load soak in staging showed 18% fewer hard rejects and a 12% reduction in KV cold misses on rejoin. See CI logs for full results.

Risk and mitigations: The main risk is control-plane amplification if circuit deltas are too chatty; mitigated by compact delta encoding and 500ms debounce. We also added resource-aware backpressure in the companion to stop broadcasting when control-plane CPU > 70%.

Related work: builds on ENG-312 (initial shedder prototype) and reuses parts of ENG-402 for warm-compatible selection. SUP-914 incident notes referenced in linked_jira.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Ops doc and rollback steps included
- [x] Feature flag gating
- [x] Metrics and tracing keys instrumented

Next steps: monitor slo.priority.request_latency and telemetry.kv_cold_miss_rate during canary; tune tranche thresholds after first 24h of canary traffic.
